claim: Spiess et al. (ICSE 2025, arXiv 2402.02047) build a calibration framework for code models and find that out-of-the-box code models are by and large not well-calibrated; Platt scaling improves calibration and reflective (verbalized) methods are inconsistent.
stance_target: L1: calibration of code models against execution/test correctness is occupied at the framework level
quoted_support: We develop a framework for evaluating the calibration of code-generating models.

breadth.confidence_families: intrinsic token probabilities, reflective/verbalized, few-shot reflective, Platt rescaling (Section III)
breadth.model_families_and_sizes: Codex, GPT-3.5 (Section on models); sizes not verified
breadth.base_vs_instruct: not present as controlled pair; few-shot uses an instruction-tuned model
breadth.post_training_stages: not verified in this pass (batch 13 read abstract and targeted passages only)
breadth.elicitation_formats: intrinsic probability; separate reflective prompt asking confidence; few-shot (Section III-B)
breadth.benchmarks: token, line, and function/test-passing completion tasks (HumanEval referenced)
breadth.label_independence: not verified in this pass (batch 13 read abstract and targeted passages only)
breadth.contamination_split: not verified in this pass (batch 13 read abstract and targeted passages only)
breadth.calibration_metrics: ECE (10 equal-width buckets), Brier score, Brier skill score against unskilled reference
